title: Platform systems & services: central team wiki, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:

This page is the central Platform Engineering team wiki for systems and services ownership, runbooks, dashboards & alerts standards, post-incident retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap (Q2 2026). It is intended as the first stop for oncall engineers, service owners, and cross-functional partners who need operational guidance, ownership boundaries, and standardized runbook/playbook artifacts.

Scope:
- Applies to production services managed by the Platform team: control-plane (platform-api), cluster-provisioning (k8s-provisioner), observability (metrics-ingest, traces-collector), and the self-service infra tooling (env-bootstrapper, infra-ops-ui).
- Excludes customer-facing product services (product-api, user-services); those have separate runbooks under the product-docs area.

Ownership & Contacts:
- Primary owner: Platform Engineering (platform-services squad)
- Oncall rotation: platform-oncall (pagerduty schedule: PLAT_ONCALL)
- PagerDuty escalation policy: 3m (ack reminder) / 15m (escalate to lead) / 60m (escalate to ENG-SRE)
- Slack channels: #platform-oncall, #platform-ops, #platform-incidents

Systems & Services Inventory (summary):
Service | Team owner | SLO (p50/p95/p99) | Primary dashboard
platform-api | platform-services | 50ms / 150ms / 350ms | Dash: platform-api-latency
k8s-provisioner | infra-automation | N/A (async) / 5min / 10min | Dash: k8s-provisioner-ops
metrics-ingest | observability | 200ms / 800ms / 2s | Dash: metrics-ingest-throughput
traces-collector | observability | 100ms / 500ms / 1.5s | Dash: traces-collector-errors
env-bootstrapper | platform-tools | N/A / 2min / 8min | Dash: env-bootstrapper-errors

For a full inventory and owners list see: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-inventory (linked).

Dashboards & Alerts (standards):
Purpose: Provide a small number of high-signal dashboards for each service: 1) Health/Errors, 2) Latency/Throughput, 3) Capacity/Resource. Every alert must map to a runbook and an owner.

Dashboard standards:
- Tooling: Grafana is the canonical dashboarding tool. Panels must use templating (cluster, namespace, service) and avoid more than 6 series per panel.
- Naming convention: <service>-<view>-<metric> (e.g., platform-api-latency).
- Dashboard lifecycle: created by service owner, reviewed quarterly with platform-ops lead.

Alerting standards:
- Primary alerting systems: Prometheus Alertmanager for infra metrics, Loki/CloudWatch for logs-driven alerts.
- Alert classifications: P0 (service down), P1 (degraded, customer impact), P2 (operational but non-customer-facing), INFO (for telemetry anomalies).
- Each alert must include: description, runbook reference link, escalation policy, and playbook snippet for mitigations.
- Use rate limiting on noisy rules and silence by deploy-tag where possible.

Example Prometheus alert (canonical format):
---
alert: PlatformAPIHighLatency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.15
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: P1
annotations:
  summary: 'platform-api 95th latency > 150ms ({{ $value }})'
  runbook: '/confluence/eng-platform/platform-api-runbook-2025'
---

Creating a new dashboard/alert (step-by-step):
1) Open Grafana -> New Dashboard -> Import JSON template from /repo/grafana/dashboards/templates.
2) Add templating variables: cluster, namespace, service. Save with team ACL = platform-services.
3) Create Prometheus rule in /repo/alerts/platform/<service>.rules.yml and open PR to platform-alerts repo.
4) Add runbook link to alert annotations and link the runbook page here.
5) Request review from observability team and platform-ops lead.

Runbooks & Incident Playbooks (template):
Every runbook must follow the same top-level sections and be discoverable from the alert annotation. Use the minimal first-step-first approach so oncall can resolve within 15 minutes for common issues.

Runbook template (required headings):
- Title (service + symptom)
- Summary (1-2 lines)
- Impact & detection (what the alert means)
- Runbook steps (ordered, concise)
- Mitigation examples (quick-fix commands)
- Escalation contact & PagerDuty schedule
- Post-incident tasks (owners for RCA)
- Related dashboards & logs links

Example quick-fix commands (do not run blindly):
- Check pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api -o wide
- Restart failing deployment: kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/platform-api --record
- Tail logs (last 2h): kubectl -n platform logs deploy/platform-api -c api --since=2h | grep ERROR | tail -n 200

On-call incident flow (high level):
1) Alert fires -> oncall acknowledges in PagerDuty and opens incident channel (#platform-incidents).
2) Triage: determine scope (single region, all clusters, degraded) and update incident header.
3) Apply mitigations from runbook (short-term).
4) If not resolved in 30m escalate per policy and page platform lead.
5) Once stable, capture timeline, impact, and owner for RCA and schedule retrospective.

Retrospectives & RCA process:
- Every P0/P1 incident requires an RCA and a 30-60 minute blameless retrospective within 5 business days.
- Template: summary, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates.
- Action items are tracked in the platform tracking board (JIRA project: PLATOPS).
- Postmortem review cadence: monthly cross-team review with Observability and infra-automation.

Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities):
- 2026-04: Migrate core dashboards to new Grafana v9 templates and switch to synthetic monitoring for platform-api end-to-end checks.
- 2026-05: Rollout autosilencing for non-actionable alerts and implement alert scoring to reduce noise by 35%.
- 2026-06: Launch platform self-service: single-click cluster provisioning in staging with RBAC onboarding flow.
- Continuous: Improve SLO coverage: add p50/p95/p99 for 80% of platform-managed services by end of Q2.

How-tos & Team wiki pointers:
- How to onboard a new service: /confluence/eng-platform/onboard-new-service-template (includes checklist: metrics, dashboards, alerts, runbook, ownership).
- How to add a PagerDuty rule & schedule: /confluence/eng-platform/pagerduty-guidelines.
- Template repos: git@internal:redwood/grafana-templates and git@internal:redwood/platform-alerts.

Governance & review cycles:
- Dashboards and alert rules are reviewed quarterly by the platform-ops lead.
- Runbooks are required to be updated after every incident; owners must confirm runbook update in the postmortem.
- SLO reviews: monthly with product reliability stakeholders.
